caseno: Appeal from Original Decree (FA) No.9 of 2000.
lawyer:
Shamim Khaled Ahmed with Md Mofizul Islam Advocates -----For the Appellant. 
Nahid Yesmin, Assistant Attorney-General -----For Proforma Defendant-Respondent NO.4.
 Mohammad Salahuddin, Advocate -----for Proforma Defendant Respondent No.5. 
Mahbubey Alam with Md Mozammel Hossain and Harun-ur-Rashid, Advocates -----For Respondent Nos. 6-12. 
Md Jakir Hossain with Khandaker Khalilur Rahman and Narayan Chandra Mondal, Advocates -----For Respondent Nos. 2 & 13.
parties:
General Manager, Bangladesh Bank ----- Appellant 
Vs.
Saiyed Shahidul Huq and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: This civil proceeding by way of First Appeal before this Court depicts a lamentable episode and an apt parading how blood of one organ of Government could be sucked by another unit of the said Government.

2. In challenge of a Judgment dated August 16, 1998 followed by a decree dismissing plaintiff's suit for a declaration of title and also for a decree of permanent injunction plaintiffs as appellants approached this Court in this First Appeal.

3. Plaintiffs are appellants and defendants are respondents to the appeal.

4. Appellants as plaintiffs on 4-3-1989 instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 87 of 1989 in first Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka for a declaration that property described in schedule-A to plaint is acquired land of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff and plaintiff's title therein is unaffected by defendants documents and also, for decree of permanent injunction restraining defendants from disturbing possession of plaintiff on schedule 'A' property, Schedule 'A' land shall be described hereinafter as suit property.

5. Lifeblood of plaint case is hereunder:

a.	Suit property along with other properties was recorded in CS Khatian No. 910 in Mouza Shahar Dhaka in the name of Raghunath Das. Suit property was requisitioned and acquired for Dhaka Improvement Trust (for short DIT) now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakhya (briefly RAJUK) under Land Acquisition Case No. 3 of 1963-64. DlT having exercised right and ownership granted lease in respect of 35 Bighas 2 Kathas and 2 Chattaks of property to plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Plaintiff Bangladesh Bank got ka lease from Government for public purpose and for economic development and, also, for building and constructing staff and officer’s quarters. Plaintiff Bank got allotment and physical possession upon management. Possession of the property was delivered on 21-12-1979. Standard Leave Agreement was executed and registered on 6-4-1981. Plaintiff Bank exercised owner-ship and took possession on leased out suit property. Plaintiff Bank constructed staff and officer’s quarters. Suit property was wrongly and fraudulently recorded in State Acquisition Khatian in SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 in the name of one Golam Hossain Rezwani.

b. Property standing in the name of Golam Hossain Rezwani mainly comprised of a glass factory and building and it was treated as an abandoned property and it was taken over by Ministry of Industries as an abandoned industry. Ministry of Industries, thereafter, transferred the property by a deed of transfer in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq as proprietor of Eastern Trading Corporation. In the deed of transfer CS Plot No. 254 corresponding to SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 had been wrongly inserted. Defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq having been unable to possess the property fraudulently sold out to defendant No.2 and other defendants preparing Block Map.

c. Defendant No. 2 and other defendants, thereafter, transferred their purchased property in favour of defendant Nos. 6-12.

d. Defendants instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 39 of 1984 through defendant No.2 Md Zulfiquer Ali Talukder for declaration of title and decree of permanent injunction.

e. Defendants after creating various fraudulent documents against the title of plaintiff Bank. Defendants and their associates threatened plaintiff Bank to make forcible entrance on suit property and illegally dispossessed plaintiff Bank and that dispossession gave rise to cause of action on part of plaintiff Bank to lay the suit before Court.

The suit was, thereafter, renumbered as Title Suit No. 64 of 1993 on transfer to the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and Fourth Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka.

6. Respondent Nos. 6-13 of the appeal had been added as defendant Nos. 6-13 in the suit, respondent No.2 and 3 as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and respondent No. 13 as added defendant No. 13 put up resistance in the suit and traversed allegations mounted against them on presentation of three separate written statements.

7. Essence of statements embodied in three sets of written statements are:

a. Suit is not maintainable without a prayer for declaration of title on suit property and, also, recovery of Khas possession thereon.

b. Plaintiff got no cause of action to lay suit.

c. Suit is barred by limitation.

d. Suit property originally belonged to Golam Hossain Rezwani and others and Golam Hossain Rezwani and others left former East Pakistan during Liberation War of Bangladesh of the year 1971 and .their whereabouts were not known and property was enlisted as Abandoned Property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972. Chief Martial Law Administrator on behalf of the Government of Bangladesh through Section Officer Ministry of Industries sold the suit property along with other properties to defendant No.1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq, proprietor of Mis Eastern Trading Corporation for valuable consideration of Taka 22,00,000 and possession had been handed over to defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq who got his name mutated in the concerned Tahsil Office, and paid rent and got rent receipts.

e. Defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq for the purpose of sale made some small plots of land and transferred the property in favour of defendant No. 2 and defendant No. 2 thereafter, sold some properties in favour of other defendants.

f. Suit land was neither requisitioned nor acquisition in Land Acquisition Case No.3 of 1963-64 and plaintiff did not acquireany title on suit properties, plaintiff Bank, also, got no possession on suit property.

8. Over pleadings of parties, following five (5) issues had been framed:

(i) Suit as framed is maintainable?

(ii) Is there any cause of action in filing the suit?

(iii) Is the suit barred by limitation?

(iv) Has the plaintiff got any title, interest and possession on the suit property?

(v) Is the plaintiff entitled to a decree as prayed for?

9. Evidence, both oral and documentary, had been led in support of the respective contentions of the parties. Two (2) witnesses got examined in support of plaintiff case and four (4)witnesses stood on the witness box to buttress the case of the defendants. Some of the documents filed from the side of defendants-respondents had not been proved in accordance with law.

10. Syed Ahmed, Deputy Director of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank stood on witness box as PW 1 in support of plaint case.

11. AKM Motiur Rahman, Deputy Director, Engineering Department, plaintiff Bank gave evidence as PW 2.

12. Haji Md Rafiqul Islam as Holder of Power of Attorney for and on behalf of defendant Nos. 6 to 11 gave evidence as DW 1.

13. Md Anwarul Haque added defendant No. 12 for himself and on behalf of defendant No.2 gave evidence as DW 2.

14. Haji Abdur Razzak and Haji Md Alauddin stood on witness box as DWs and 4 respectively. They are witnesses on factum of possession.

15. Learned Subordinate Judge did not decide Issue No.1 in the strict term of the issue framed. Learned Subordinate Judge his directed his approach on the legal character of General Manager of plaintiff Bank to lay the suit and held that General Manager got no legal character to file the suit on behalf of Bangladesh Bank.

16. Learned Subordinate Judge decided Issue No. 11 in the negative and found that the plaintiff did not state in plaint on which date defendant forcibly entered into the suit property and dispossessed plaintiff and it could not be ascertained on which date the cause of action arose.

17. Learned Subordinate Judge also, decided Issue No. III in the negative and held that plaintiff had been aware of preparation of SA Record of Right in respect of suit property and being aware of wrong record did not present suit within proper time and suit stood barred by limitation.

18. Learned Subordinate Judge, also, decided Issue No. IV against the plaintiff and held that plaintiff failed to prove title and possession on suit property.

19. Learned Subordinate Judge, also, held that plaintiff failed to produce relevant papers and documents in support of right of DIT to acquire any  property without prior permission of Government of Bangladesh and, also, right to lease out property in favour of any institution.

20. Learned Subordinate Judge with the above decisions dismissed the suit.

21. Plaintiff having been resentful of the above adjudication sought setting aside those through medium of this first appeal before this Court.

22. Contentions pressed into service from the side of plaintiff-appellant are catalogued hereunder:

i. Government as acquiring body did acquire the suit property along with other properties of requiring body Dhaka Improvement Trust and acquisition was complete on publication of Gazette Notification, Exhibit-2, Plaintiff Bank acquired title on suit property by way of lease deed, Exhibit-3 and, thereafter by way of demarcation and layout plan, Exhibit-4 and Exhibit-4(Ka) respectively and suit property could not be treated as abandoned property and also leased out by Ministry of Industries to one Saiyed Shahidul Huq defendant No. 1 and the lease matter and subsequent deeds of transfer by defendant No. 1 to other defendants are absolutely void, illegal and without jurisdiction and learned Judge failed to take into account the legal implications of Gazette Notification, lease deed and deeds of title and possession of plaintiff Bank and committed a substantial error of law in the decisions.

ii. Enlistment of suit property as abandoned property and sale deed by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No.1. and subsequent transfer of suit property by defendant No. 1 in favour of other defendants could not in any way affect title of plaintiff and learned judge did not take into account this legal aspect and, thus, fell into a serious error of law in not awarding decree in favour of plaintiff-appellant.

iii. Suit was not at all barred by limitation and suit was well within time and decision of learned judge on point of limitation is ex facie, contrary to materials on record and decision on limitation cannot be sustained in law.

iv. Plaintiff Bank got delivery of possession upon layout plan and demarcation and admittedly in possession of a substantial portion of the acquired and leased out property and plaintiff Bank paid advalorem court fee and the suit was not even barred by limitation, plaintiff bank was entitled to relief of recovery of possession of portion of property if found to be out of possession and learned Judge committed a patent illegality in his decision in dismissing the suit.

v. Property on which Golam Hossain Rezwani stood was outside acquired property and State Acquisition Record of Right had been wrongly prepared and wrong record cannot in any way affect legality and validity of acquisition of property and acquisition proceeding was not challenged from side of defendants on institution of suit and learned Judge erred in holding that plaintiff Bank's title under acquisition by Government was not affected by documents allegedly created by defendants.

vi. Bangladesh Bank is the plaintiff and Bank has been stated to be represented by General Manager and misdescription, if any, could not make plaintiff out of court and the substance and not the form of suit was required to be gone into by learned Judge and amendment sought by plaintiff in this respect was refused by learned Judge and dismissal of suit on question of legal character of plaintiff Bank is absolutely illegal and decision cannot be sustained in law.

23. Contentions advanced from side of plaintiff appellant had been adopted by defendant-Fifth- respondent, Chairman former DIT now RAJUK.

i. Golam Hossain Rezwani having been the rightful owner of suit property same had been correctly recorded in his name and Golam Hossain Rezwani during war of liberation of Bangladesh left for Pakistan and the property had been enlisted as abandoned property and Ministry of Industries took over the management of glass factory and then transferred the suit factory in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq who took over possession of suit property and being owner in possession of suit property by way of sale deeds transferred property in favour of other defendants and some of the transferee defendants transferred their purchased property to other defendants and defendants acquired good title and possession over suit property.

ii.	In a suit for permanent injunction exclusive possession of party seeking permanent injunction is required to be proved and plaintiff-appellant failed to prove exclusive possession over suit property and, on the other hand, defendant-respondents through evidences, oral and documentary, proved possession of defendants over suit property. Defendants got their names mutated in record of right and paid rents and receipts are evidences of possession of defendants.

iii.	Suit was barred by limitation and learned Judge was well justified in dismissing suit on point of limitation.

iv. Bangladesh Bank did not come forward to be plaintiff and General Manager, Bangladesh Bank could not be plaintiff for Bangladesh Bank.

25. In the wake of rival contentions advanced from the Bar, points that survive for determination are:

1. (a)Whether suit property is acquired property of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff Bank. and

(b) Whether title, interest and possession of plaintiff-appellant's Bank on suit property have been affected by subsequent treatment of suit property as abandoned property and also, by deeds of transfer by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No. 1 and subsequent deeds of conveyances by defendant No. 1 to other defendants.

2. Whether suit stood barred by limitation.

3. Whether suit can be thrown away on point that General Manger, Bangladesh Bank filed the suit.

4.(a) Whether the decisions rendered by Trial Judge in dismissing plaintiff Bank's suit can be sustained and those are susceptible to be overturned and

(b) Whether plaintiff Bank can be graced with reliefs prayed for.

26. Points formulated now may be approached and resolved.

27. Point No.1 plaintiff bank traced its title on the strength of an allotment and the execution and registration of a lease deed from former DIT now RAJUK who is said to have acquired property in dispute in a Requisition and Acquisition proceeding.

28. Plaintiff Bank put forward claim that DIT in Land Acquisition Case No.3 of 1963-64 acquired 14, 2118 acres equivalent to 43 big has of property from full of CS Plot Nos. 253, 254, 255, 256, 258, 259, 260 and part of CS plot No. 235 under sheet No. 76 and full of CS plot Nos. 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 under sheet No. 78 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, Police Station Sutrapur, District Dhaka. Requisition proceeding was on 28-5-1963, property was acquired on 18-11-1965. Acquisition was concluded and reached to its finality on Notification in Gazette on 25-11-1965 (Exhibit-2) DIT allotted 35 bighas 2 kahtas and 2 chataks of property in favour of plaintiff Bank on 21-12-1979 Standard Lease Agreement by  DIT in favour of plaintiff Bank was on 15-4-1981 (Exhibit-3), plaintiff Bank took over possession of leased out property on 21-12-1979 (Exhibit-4). plaintiff Bank's property faced dispute in respect of CS Plot No. 254 converting an area of .61 acres and this 0.61 acres of property is the suit property. CS Plot No. 254 corresponds to SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 and SA Record of the two (2) plots had been prepared in the name of Golam Hossain Rezwani and the said record of right has been challenged as wrong by plaintiff Bank. Plaintiff Bank asserted that treating suit property as abandoned property is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction and transfer of the property by Ministry of Industry in favour of defendant No. 1 and transfer by defendant No. 1 by way of deeds of transfer in favour of other defendants are also illegal and void and defendants did not acquire any title on suit property and title of plaintiff Bank on suit property had not been at all affected by said deeds of transfer.

29. Defendants-respondents rested their claim on the basis of a deed of sale by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq and Ministry said its right to transfer by way of sale deeds on the strength that the property was an abandoned property as abandoned by recorded owner Golam Hossain Rezwani. Defendant No.1 being the owner by a good number of deeds transferred property to other defendants and transferee defendants, thereafter, again sold their purchased property to another group of defendants.

30. Exhibit-1 is Cadastral Survey Record of Right containing CS Plot No. 254 (in full) measuring an area of .61 acres, Exhibit-2 is Gazate Notification dated 25-11-1965 and Gazette Notification was published in exercise of power conferred by sub-section (b) of section 93A of Town Improvement Act XIII of 1953 (Act of 1953). In schedule noted in Gazette Notification CS plot No. 254 (in full) are being more or less 14.2118 acres along with other plots had been listed. Exhibit-3 is Standard Lease Agreement dated 6-4-1981 for residential property between Dhaka Improvement Trust on the one part who is called the Lessor and Manager Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka referred to as Lessee or the other part. In schedule of Lease Agreement, area of property leased out is 35 bighas, 2 kathas and 2 chhataks which is equivalent 11-2/3 acres CS plot No. 254 (in full) is suit plot. Suit plot No. 254 (in full ) along with other plots (full or part) had been noted in the schedule. Exhibit-4 is final survey performed by Dhaka Improvement Trust in respect of leased out 35 bighas, 2 kathas and 2 chhataks. Final survey had been performed on 21-12-1979. Exhibit 4(Ka) is map showing CS Plot No. 254 and other leased out plots.

31. Town Improvement Act, 1953 had undergone massive amendments by way of Town Improvement (Amendment) Act, 1987 which came into force on 30th April, 1987.

32. Relevant provisions of section 93A (1) and 93A(3) and 93A (4)(b) of The Act of 1953 before amendment by Town Improvement (Amendment) Act 1987 are meditated and now conveniently pressed in aid in resolving the controversy.

33. Section 93A(1) enjoined that if in the opinion of Provincial Government it was expedient or necessary so to do, for construction, betterment of roads, waterways or any other communications and the developments of areas for residential, commercial, industrial purpose or for establishment of parks, playing fields and open space for relief of congestion in any area to which this Act extends Provincial Government might, by order in writing, requisition any property for the Board and could make such further order as might appear to Government necessary or expedient in connection with such requisition.

34. Section 93A(3) postulated that when order of requisition had been served under sub-section (2) in respect of a property provincial Government might direct District Magistrate to take and deliver possession of property within 2 weeks to the Board and Board might use or deal with property as might appear to it to be expedient.

35. Section 93A(4)(h) enshrined that provincial Government would publish in Official Gazette a notice to the effect that provincial Government had decided to acquire requisitioned property for Board and on and from beginning of the day on which the notice was published, requisitioned property would vest absolutely to Board free from all encumbrance and period of such requisition of such property would come to an end.

36. From above it has become crystallised that with the publication in Official Gazette in respect of an acquired property by way of requisition and acquisition proceeding, requisitioned and acquired property would vest absolutely to Board free from all encumbrances.

37. Exhibit-Kha is the list of properties taken over by Ministry of Industries and in serial No. 556 there is nothing manifesting that MS Dhaka Glass Works and Cork Industries had been taken as an abandoned property. Date of taking over is noted on 19-4-1972. Exhibit - Uma is deed of sale dated 8-7-1982 between MS Eastern Trading Corporation, represented by its sole proprietor Mr Saiyed Shahidul Huq (defendant No.1) of First Part and Chief Martial Law Administrator, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by MK Zaman, Section Officer, Ministry of Industries and Commerce of Second Part, Exhibit-Gha is certificate of taking over and making over physical possession of Dhaka Glass Works by defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq figuring himself as Administrator, Dhaka Glass Works. The date is 25-3-1980. Exhibits Cha-1 and Cha-2 are two Rent Receipts of the year 1984 showing payment of rent in respect of State Acquisition Khatian No. 4836. Exhibit Jhaha is certified copy of irrevocable General Power of Attorney by defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq in favour of Md Motiur Rahman Rentu empowering the latter to execute and register any document including deed of transfer. Exhibits-Cheha-1, Ja,Tha-1, Tha-3, Tha-4, Tha-5, Tha-6, Tha-10, Tha-11, Tha-12, Da-2 and Da-3 are deeds of defendants who are transferees and subsequent transferees from defendant No. 1.

<u>38. Admittedly, alleged taking over of suit property as abandoned property either by Ministry of Works or by Ministry of Industries was much later than Gazette Notification published by Government giving finality to requisition and acquisition proceeding when suit property absolutely vested with Government free from all encumbrances as mandated by section 93A(4)(h) of the Town Improvement Act of 1953. The property which vested with the Government i.e. Dhaka Improvement Trust, free from all encumbrances cannot at all vest subsequently with any other organ of the Government either Ministry of Works or Ministry of Industries under the garb of abandoned property.</u>

39. Dhaka Improvement Trust, an important organ of Government, entered into a lease agreement with plaintiff Bangladesh Bank, another important limb of Government and date of Lease Agreement is 6-4-1981. Sale deed in favour of defendant No.1 by Ministry of Industries is dated 8-7-1982 which is, also, much later than Lease Agreement between Dhaka Improvement Trust and plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Plaintiff Bangladesh Bank, thus, acquired title and interest in suit property before alleged acquisition of any right and interest by defendant No. 1 and by deeds of conveyances, mutations and payment of rents and other acts performed by defendants, which were much later acts, cannot affect at all the right, title and interest and possession of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank in any way and right, title and interest and possession of plaintiff Bank remained and remain unaffected.

40. Exhibit-Ka is certified copy of State Acquisition Khatian No. 4836 standing in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani, No documents had been produced from side of defendant-respondents to show basis of preparation of State Acquisition Record of Right in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani. Mere State Acquisition Record of Right in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani is no evidence of title. It had earlier been stated that defendants respondents, also, failed to produce any documentary evidence manifesting that suit property was declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972.

41. Exhibit-5 is photocopy of certified copy of Judgment recorded in Title Suit No. 39 of 1984 of Sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit. Defendant No.2 Md Zulfiqar Ali Talukder had been plaintiff and Bangladesh Bank had been defendant No. 1 and former DIT now RAJUK had been defendant No.2 and the suit was for decree of permanent injunction in respect of plaintiff's purchased property from defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq. Suit was dismissed by judgment dated 23-11-1989 and judgment was followed by a decree. Learned Assistant Judge in recording dismissal of suit positively found that plaintiff of suit failed to prove possession in suit property.

42. Exhibit-5(ka) is certified copy of Title Appeal No. 39 of 1990 of First Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka and appeal was carried by plaintiff of suit Md Zulfiquar Ali Talukder having felt aggrieved of judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 39 of 1984. Learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka by Judgment dated 31-8-1995 dismissed appeal and maintained judgment and decree passed by learned Assistant Judge. In dismissing appeal learned Additional District Judge recorded following decisions, amongst others:

(a) Plaintiff (Md Zulfiqar Ali Talukder) could not produce any title showing that Golam Hossain Rezwani was owner of suit property and plaintiff only filed certified copy of State Acquisition Khatian in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani which is no evidence of title.

(b) Plaintiff failed to produce any Gazette Notification showing that suit property was declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972.

(c) Plaintiff failed to prove that suit property belonged to Golam Hossain Rezwani and it was declared as abandoned property and

(d) CS plot No. 254 i.e. suit plot was acquired by Government in November, 1965. Deed of Lease dated 15A-1981 shows that entire CS Plot No. 254 and other plots were leased out in favour of Bangladesh Bank. Delivery of possession Certificate, Plan approved by DIT, Mouza Map of Sutrapur etc. show that defendant (Bangladesh Bank) became owner of suit property in 1981 by taking lease from DIT i.e. prior to alleged purchase of plaintiff's vendor.

<u>43. In view of discussion made above conclusion that can safely be reached is that ,suit property is acquired property of Government and it was legally leased out to plaintiff Bank whose right, title, interest and possession on suit property had not been at all affected by defendants-respondent's sale deeds, mutations and payment of rents.</u>

44. Point No.2: Plaintiff Bank sought reliefs in the following terms:

(a) a decree be passed declaring that the land described in schedule-A to the plaint is acquired land of the Government and legally leased out: to the plaintiff and plaintiff’s title therein is not affected by defendant’s documents.

(b) Defendants be restrained permanently from disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land.

45. DIT leased out suit property along with other properties under acquisition in favour of plaintiff Bank by way of Lease document dated 15-4-1981. Plaintiff claimed to have entered into possession of suit property and defendant No.1 claimed title and possession on suit property on the strength of a deed of sale from Ministry of Industries on 8-9-1982 and the other defendant's title rested on sale deed dated 8-9-1982. Plaintiff Bank's suit had been laid on 22-4-1985 and claim put forward from side of defendants was definitely not before 8-9-1982 and surely after 8-9-1982. Suit had been, therefore, presented well within time and could not be at all said to have been barred by limitation.

<u>46. This takes us to finding reached by trial judge on limitation. Learned Judge found that plaintiff had been aware of preparation of wrong record in respect of suit property and being aware of the, wrong record did not lay suit within stipulated time and there was no cause of action of suit and suit stood barred by limitation. Finding reached by learned Judge on limitation is absolutely wrong. Knowledge of wrong record of right can be starting point of limitation and a litigant public even if aware of wrong record of a record of right can wait and wait till his right is invaded by other side and his suit will be well within time if he institutes Suit within six years from date when his right on suit property is denied and invaded by other party. This view of ours is fortified with three authorities. Raj Kiran Chandra Roy Bahadur and others vs Tarak Nath Gongopadhyay and others, 40 CW No. 566, Abdul Hafez and another vs Lal Miah and others, 1988 BLD 497 and Banghadar Mitra and others vs Natabar Sardar, being dead & others, 1 BCR 393. In the case in hand the plaintiff Bank laid the suit within the period of limitation and it cannot be said as of Trial Judge that suit stood barred by limitation. Point No; 2 stands answered in negative.</u>

47. Point No.3: Examination of Lease Agreement, Exhibit-S indicates that the Lease Agreement had been between DIT on the one part and BM Ahmed, Manager Bangladesh Bank of the other part and all transactions in respect of Lease Agreement had been performed by General Manager on behalf of Bangladesh Bank. In the suit in hand General Manager of Bangladesh Bank laid the suit. Bangladesh Bank is an organ of the Government Order. XXIX, rule 1 enjoins that in any suit by or against Government, the plaint or written statement shall be signed by such person as the Government may by general or special order appoint in this behalf and shall be verified by the person whom the Government may so appoint and who is acquainted with the fact of the case. General Manager having signed the Lease Agreement for Bangladesh Bank, he laid suit in Court. Plaintiff’s suit cannot be thrown away on ground that General Manager filed suit. Bangladesh Bank is represented by General Manager, defect is merely a technical one and not at all substantial and technicality must be to cause of justice. Point No. 3 also, stands answered in firm negative.

48. Point No. 4(a) : One of reasons found favour with Trial Judge in dismissing plaintiff's suit was that plaintiff failed to produce any paper evidencing that DIT without obtaining permission from Government of Bangladesh could acquire any property and also, could enter into Lease Agreement with any institution. The said reason canvassed by learned Trial Judge was absolutely misconceived inasmuch as DIT did not acquire any property and it is former East Pakistan Government who acquired suit property along with other properties Government was Requiring Body and DIT was Requiring Body. Acquiring Authority Government on asking of Requiring Body DIT acquired property for Requiring Body DIT and DIT thereafter being owner of suit property leased out property in favour of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Exhibit-2, Gazette Notification is best evidence demonstrating that suit property along with other properties stood acquired by Government for DIT.

49. Other ground taken by learned Trial Judge in dismissing suit was that no date had been stated in plaint indicating defendant's forcible entrance into suit property and, as such, it could not be gathered on which date cause of action of suit arose.

<u>50. Expression "cause of action means entire bundle of facts a plaintiff has to prove in order to be eligible for grant of relief. It can, also be said that cause of action pre-supposed the existence of a right in plaintiff which right has either been infringed or is threatened to be infringed. Cause of action cannot be construed in an isolated way and whole averments made in plaint are to be seen and taken together to see whether any cause of action has been disclosed or not. It is the plaint as a whole which is to be construed and not terminology or, for that matter, a few stray references.</u>

51. True it is that no specific date had been stated in plaint when defendant and associates threatened to enter into suit property forcibly and illegally dispossessed plaintiff from suit property. In paragraph No. 11 of plaint it had been simply stated that cause of action of suit arose while defendants and associates threatened to forcibly enter into suit land and illegally dispossessed plaintiff from suit property.

52. Specific date of threatened dispossession had not been noted down in plaint but that cannot be characterised to be a fundamental defect and infirmity in plaint. It cannot be at all suggested that plaint did not consist of material facts giving rise to a cause of action on the part of plaintiff to lay suit in Court. Decision of learned Trial Judge on question of non-disclosure of cause of action cannot be sustained in law.

53. Regard being had to above discussion we are of this considered view that decisions reached by learned Judge in dismissing suit cannot be sustained in law and thus stand overturned.

54. Point No. 4(b): Point No. 4(b) is surviving point in appeal. In disposing Point No.1 it has been posited that plaintiff Bank acquired title on suit property and title and interest of plaintiff Bank on .suit property cannot be at all affected by deed of sale in favour of defendant No. 1 and other deeds of sale in favour of other defendants from defendant No.1 Plaintiff through documentary evidence, Exhibit- 4(Ka) proved act of taking possession on suit property along with other properties. Defendant No.1 did not come forward to .support case that suit property was treated as abandoned property and subsequent deed of transfer in his favour by Ministry of Industries and his transfer by way of deeds of conveyances to other defendants were legal. Defendant No.2, also, did not stand on witness box though he filed written statement. DW 2 as defendant No. 12 for himself and for defendant No. 2 gave evidence. DW 2 got no right or authority to give testimony in favour of defendant No. 2 unless he was authorised with a Power of Attorney. From the above the irresistible decision that can be safely rendered is that plaintiff Bank can be graced with decree declaring that property described in schedule "A" to plaint i.e. suit property, is acquired property of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff Bank and plaintiff Bank's title is unaffected by defendant's documents.

55. It comes out from testimonies of DW 2 who is added defendant No. 12 that he got a kutcha house on suit property and defendant Nos. 6-9 got four(4) kutch a houses and defendant No. 10 got shop. It also, came out from mouth of DW 3 and DW 4 that in suit property there were three (3) shops and six (6) kutcha houses. Possession, if any, of defendant on a portion of suit property by way of construction of shops and kutch a houses, that possession is not lawful and possession is absolutely illegal and unauthorised. Defendant could not acquire any right, title and interest on suit property on basis of deeds of conveyance. which were much later than the title deed of plaintiff Bank.

56. In a suit for Permanent Injunction, factum of possession in fundamental and plaintiff can be graced with a decree of permanent injunction in respect of the suit property if he can prove exclusive possession over suit property. It has earlier stated that possession by way of construction of shops and kutcha houses, three and six in number respectively, no matter whether possession of defendants were lawful or not but it became evident that plaintiff got no possession in some portion of suit property. It is no where in plaint that plaintiff had been threatened with dispossession on a particular portion of suit property arid no evidence, as came forth from the mouth of PW 1 and PW 2 on which portion of suit property plaintiff was threatened with dispossession. It cannot be , thus, said that plaintiff Bank succeeded in proving its exclusive possession on suit property to be graced with a decree of Permanent Injunction restraining defendants respondents from entering into suit property. Plaintiff, thus, cannot be granted a decree of Permanent Injunction.

57. This takes us to petition presented by defendant Nos. 6-12 respondent sunder Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for admitting certified copies of two sale deeds executed ot1:5-3-1984 and 30-9-1986 as additional evidence and making those as Exhibits for canvassing ground that due to inadvertence and bonafide mistake said deeds had not been filed in trial Court. Hearing of First Appeal commenced on 27-4-2003 and hearing occupied a good number of days i.e. 28-4-2003, 12-5-2003, 17-5-2003, 18-5-2003, 21-5-2003, 26-5- 2003, 27-5-2003, 17-6-2003 and 18-6-2003. Hearing came to an end on 18-6-2003. Defendant respondents slept and slept for all the days of hearing and woke up only on 18-6-2003 and on that date affidavit was sworn. It was too late in the day for the defendant-respondents in filing the petition .There had been serious laches and unpardonable delay on the part of defendant-respondents in presenting petition. Moreover, grounds urged are not satisfactory. The petition has not been also prepared happily and carelessness has' been demonstrated. No. grounds exist in allowing the petition. Petition is rejected.
